letters.name: A
letters.memoryTrick: Like the 'a' in 'father' — open your mouth wide and let the sound out. It's the same long, open 'ah' you'd say at the doctor's office.

letters.name: Be
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'b' in 'baby' — a crisp, voiced pop of the lips. Same as English, but at the end of a word it hardens to a 'p' sound.

letters.name: Ce
letters.memoryTrick: Mostly found in loanwords. Before 'e' or 'i' it's 'ts' like in 'bits'; otherwise tends to be 'k'. Think of it as the 'ts' in 'cats'.

letters.name: De
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'd' in 'dog' — tongue taps behind your top teeth. At the end of a word it hardens to a 't' sound, so 'Hund' sounds like 'Hunt'.

letters.name: E
letters.memoryTrick: Long 'e' is like the 'ay' in 'play' but without the glide. Short 'e' is like the 'e' in 'bet'. It's also the unstressed 'uh' at the end of many words like 'Tasse'.

letters.name: Ef
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'f' in 'fish' — bottom lip against top teeth, air pushed through. The same sound in English and German.

letters.name: Ge
letters.memoryTrick: Always a hard 'g' like in 'goat' — never soft like 'giraffe'. At the end of a word it hardens to a 'k' sound, so 'Tag' sounds like 'Tahk'.

letters.name: Ha
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'h' in 'house' — a breathy puff at the start of a word. When it appears after a vowel, it's silent and just makes the vowel longer (like 'gehen').

letters.name: I
letters.memoryTrick: Long 'i' is like 'ee' in 'see' — smile wide. Short 'i' is like the 'i' in 'bit'. Don't confuse it with 'ie' which also makes the 'ee' sound.

letters.name: Jot
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'y' in 'yes' — never like the English 'j' in 'jam'. Think 'yoghurt', not 'judge'. The letter name itself starts with this 'y' sound: 'yot'.

letters.name: Ka
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'k' in 'kite' — sharp and unvoiced. Unlike English, German 'k' is always aspirated at the start of a word, with a little puff of air.

letters.name: El
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'l' in 'love' — tongue tip against the ridge behind your top teeth. In German, it's always a clear 'light l', never the dark 'ull' of English 'ball'.

letters.name: Em
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'm' in 'mother' — lips together, sound through the nose. Same as English in every way.

letters.name: En
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'n' in 'nose' — tongue behind top teeth, air through the nose. Same as English.

letters.name: O
letters.memoryTrick: Long 'o' is like the 'o' in 'go' but purer — round your lips and hold it steady, no glide. Short 'o' is like the 'o' in 'pot'.

letters.name: Pe
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'p' in 'pen' — with a strong puff of air at the start of a word. Hold your hand in front of your mouth and you should feel the burst.

letters.name: Qu
letters.memoryTrick: Always followed by 'u' in German, and pronounced like 'kv' — like the 'qu' in 'question' but with a sharper 'v' sound. Think 'kv' not 'kw'.

letters.name: Er
letters.memoryTrick: The classic German 'r' — a soft gargle in the back of the throat, like a gentle French 'r'. At the end of a syllable it turns into a soft vowel-like sound, almost like 'uh'.

letters.name: Es
letters.memoryTrick: At the start of a word before a vowel, it's a soft 'z' like in 'zebra'. Before 'p' or 't', it's 'sh'. Everywhere else it's the hissing 's' of 'snake'.

letters.name: Te
letters.memoryTrick: Like 't' in 'top' — tongue taps behind the teeth with a puff of air. More aspirated than English 't', so you'll feel a little burst of breath.

letters.name: U
letters.memoryTrick: Long 'u' is like 'oo' in 'moon' — round your lips tightly. Short 'u' is like the 'oo' in 'foot' but shorter. Don't mix this up with 'ü'.

letters.name: Vau
letters.memoryTrick: Usually pronounced like 'f' in 'father' (Vater, Vogel, viel). In loanwords it can sound like English 'v' (Vase, November). The letter name 'Vau' rhymes with 'cow'.

letters.name: We
letters.memoryTrick: Pronounced like English 'v' — never like the English 'w' in 'water'. Think 'Volkswagen' where 'w' sounds like 'v'. Your top teeth touch your bottom lip.

letters.name: Ix
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'x' in 'box' — the 'ks' sound. Quite rare in German, mostly found in loanwords from Greek and Latin.

letters.name: Üpsilon
letters.memoryTrick: Usually pronounced like German 'ü' — say 'ee' and round your lips. In loanwords from English it keeps its 'y' sound (Yoga, Yacht). The letter name is 'Üpsilon'.

letters.name: Zet
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'ts' in 'cats' or 'bits' — never like the English 'z' in 'zebra'. Think 'pizza' — that 'zz' is exactly the German 'z' sound.

letters.name: A-Umlaut
letters.memoryTrick: Like the 'e' in 'bed' or 'ai' in 'fair' — open your mouth like you're saying 'ah' but flatten your tongue like you're saying 'eh'. If you can't type it, write 'ae'.

letters.name: O-Umlaut
letters.memoryTrick: Like the 'i' in 'bird' or the French 'eu' in 'deux'. Say 'eh' and then round your lips tightly as if you're about to whistle. If you can't type it, write 'oe'.

letters.name: U-Umlaut
letters.memoryTrick: Say 'ee' as in 'see', then round your lips like you're saying 'oo'. It's exactly the French 'u' in 'tu'. If you can't type it, write 'ue'.

letters.name: Eszett / Sharp S
letters.memoryTrick: Sounds exactly like a sharp hissing 'ss' — think of the hiss of a snake. It only appears after long vowels and diphthongs. Switzerland doesn't use it; they always write 'ss'.

letters.name: Ce-Ha
letters.memoryTrick: Two sounds depending on the vowel before it: after 'i', 'e', 'ä', 'ö', 'ü' it's soft like the 'h' in 'huge' (tongue against the roof of your mouth). After 'a', 'o', 'u' it's scratchy like the 'ch' in Scottish 'loch' (in the back of your throat).

letters.name: Es-Ce-Ha
letters.memoryTrick: Exactly like 'sh' in 'shoe' or 'shop'. Once you know 'sch', you've unlocked one of the most common German sound patterns.

letters.name: E-I
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'eye' or the 'i' in 'mine' — always this sound, no exceptions. Think of 'Einstein' — the 'ei' in his name is the classic German 'eye' sound.

letters.name: I-E
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'ee' in 'see' — a long, smiling 'ee' sound. Remember: in German, 'ie' says 'ee' and 'ei' says 'eye'. The second letter tells you what to say!

letters.name: E-U
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'oy' in 'boy' or 'toy' — round your lips as if saying 'oh' and then quickly glide to 'ee'. Think of saying 'Europa' with a proud 'oy' sound.
